annotations.text:
OPTION A — Chat-first copilot

The conversation is the product. Project context sits on the left; every command and approval appears inline in the thread.

Best when: one person, one task at a time, exploratory work.
Tradeoff: no overview. With 3 agents and 12 changes a day you cannot see the state of the system, only the last thing you talked about. Approvals scroll away.

OPTION B — Changes feed (mission control)   ← my recommendation

The Change is the unit of work. The feed is the hero; chat is docked as an input, not the centre. Awaiting-approval rows are pinned and colour-coded.

Best when: several agents and humans acting on shared infrastructure — you always see what is pending, applied, drifted or failed.
Tradeoff: less immersive for a long single conversation; the chat panel is narrow.

OPTION C — Three-pane cockpit

An IDE for operations: explorer, tabbed work area, chat, and a trace drawer along the bottom. Familiar to anyone using Cursor or VS Code.

Best when: deep hands-on work — reading diffs, editing terraform, following a trace.
Tradeoff: the densest and most intimidating of the four; the tab metaphor hides what is not open, so pending approvals are easy to miss.

OPTION D — Change pipeline

Changes flow left to right: Proposed → Preview ready → Awaiting approval → Applying → Done. Feels like a CD pipeline, so the approval gate is spatial.

Best when: a team wants a shared board and an obvious queue; great on a wall screen.
Tradeoff: columns waste space when volume is low, and it is a poor host for a long chat or a big diff — those need a detail view anyway.

NEW PROJECT — the feature I would build the product around

Picking tools does not just install binaries: it GENERATES the guardrails. Choose Terraform and you get plan-pinning plus approval on apply/destroy; choose Kubernetes and you get gates on delete/scale/patch; each tool declares the credentials it needs and the hosts it may reach.

Onboarding a project goes from a day of hand-written YAML to five minutes of clicking — and the result is safer than most people would write themselves. Everything stays editable before Create.

CHANGE DETAIL — where trust is actually earned

One screen answers every question a human has before saying yes: what exactly changes (pinned diff), who asked (agent, via MCP), which policy rule gated it, what the blast radius is, which credential was used (by name — value seen by nobody), and what the revert looks like if it goes wrong.

The steps list shows the agent's whole plan with the gated step called out, so you approve a plan rather than a black box. Promotion to prod is offered only after it is healthy in staging.
